touches.text: It is the only daemon in the system
it launches a script in each device's cairn/devices/<device>/groundloop called pulse.py, each as its own process.
It writes one JSON record at the end of a pass with a list of each device: beat time, found device (folder), NOT FOUND or name, file mtime, pid it spawned. It does no checks and no takeover.

Beat interval is a setting, 60 s for now. It was held at 60 s while too much hung off the ground loop; that is cleaned up, and we expect to go a lot faster later (Akien: "faster than once a second"). (Q#15, Akien 2026-11-03)

Cairn keeps a list of scheduled things (the scheduler, 5.8). Each ground loop pulse, its shim has Cairn check that list against the clock: no match (eg 2245), the pulse is dropped; a match (eg 2300) is a PROBE, and it kicks off that thing in the Cairn device.
Sleep's base trigger is the clock (2300). Once we can tell how recently things were interacted with, that overrides the base clock. (Q#10, Akien 2026-11-03)
The bus makes this messaging inspectable, the messages show on the bus' web panel as a "Murderbot Diaries" "Public Feed" the operator can review for purposes such as diagnostics.
pulse.py is part of the shim. The ground loop calling it tells the shim the pulse has arrived, and starts the shim if it isn't running.
